verdictReason: One HIGH requirement completeness gap: immutable human activation attribution is not defined in persisted schedule/occurrence contract. Two MEDIUM internal contract gaps require deferred-occurrence interruption semantics and fixed-versus-configurable cadence alignment. These are local specification fixes, not unmet production release evidence.

issues.description: FR-11 requires the human activator recorded separately from background principal, and FR-10 requires immutable activation provenance. Frozen storage specifies principal/revision/version and mutable schedule update audit, but no durable human actor/time for a normal clean Resume. Uncertainty acknowledgment actor/time only records activations with uncertainty; it cannot supply attribution for all activations or historical accepted occurrences.
issues.suggestion: Aria must freeze an immutable activation event record or equivalent explicit persisted activation actor/time snapshots covering every successful activation, including an empty uncertainty set. Define principal, environment, confirmed revision and version linkage from accepted occurrences; preserve previous attribution after edits, clean Resume and removal/recreation. Add migration/API or linked audit projection and PostgreSQL provenance tests. Align contract, spec and associated story before critique2.

issues.description: DEFERRED occurrences retain nominal identity and must eventually settle at grace expiry, but pause/removal/configuration edit and Resume reset schedule eligibility/cursor with no frozen transition for an outstanding deferred occurrence. The ordinary due poller will no longer revisit that old nominal slot, leaving truthful history indefinitely marked delayed.
issues.suggestion: Freeze one bounded interruption rule under test→schedule→occurrence locking: settle an outstanding deferred identity without execution when pause/remove/configuration mutation supersedes it, with explicit stable decision code and immutable grace/provenance. Specify behavior during capability disable and later reenable. Add pause/remove/edit/resume-versus-deferral race and post-grace history tests; align API codes, contract and story.

issues.description: ASM-01 and OQ-04 describe a configurable 60-second minimum, whereas the frozen resolver contract and capabilities expose a fixed 60-second floor established by zero-second minute grammar. Higher configurable floors require additional correct bounded validation and are not established by that grammar proof.
issues.suggestion: Align requirements/spec/research/contract on fixed 60-second floor for this implementation and retain different production cadence as a future adopted contract, or explicitly specify and test bounded higher-floor validation. Keep configurable grace distinct from cadence floor; do not imply an unsupported configurability guarantee.

nextAction: Halt implementation; return to architect/PM for revised local contract/spec and associated story, then independent mandatory COMPLEX critique2. External production grant/pilot/load evidence stays release-gated, not a local revision blocker.
